berliner-luftbruecke#summary: After the Soviet blockade of West Berlin, the Western powers supply the city from the air for almost a year.
berliner-luftbruecke#text: When the Western powers introduced the deutschmark in their zones in June 1948, the Soviet Union closed all roads, railways and waterways to West Berlin in order to push the Western Allies out of the city. The United States and Britain thereupon set up an airlift: in almost 280,000 flights the raisin bombers brought around 2.3 million tons of coal, food and medicine to the roughly two million Berliners. On 12 May 1949 Stalin lifted the blockade. The airlift turned the occupiers into protectors in the eyes of many Germans, led to the founding of NATO in 1949 and accelerated the emergence of the Federal Republic and the GDR in the same year.
gruendung-israels#summary: David Ben-Gurion proclaims the State of Israel; the first Arab-Israeli war begins.
gruendung-israels#text: In 1947 the United Nations had decided to partition the British mandate territory of Palestine into a Jewish and an Arab state. On 14 May 1948 Ben-Gurion proclaimed the independence of Israel, which after the Holocaust offered a home to many survivors. The neighboring Arab states attacked at once, Israel held its ground and enlarged its territory. Around 700,000 Palestinians fled or were driven out; the refugee question and the borders remain at the heart of the Middle East conflict to this day.
ausrufung-volksrepublik-china#title: Proclamation of the People's Republic of China
ausrufung-volksrepublik-china#summary: After victory in the civil war, Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic in Beijing.
ausrufung-volksrepublik-china#text: The civil war between Mao's communists and the nationalists under Chiang Kai-shek ended in 1949 with the withdrawal of the nationalists to Taiwan. On 1 October Mao proclaimed the founding of the People's Republic from the Gate of Heavenly Peace. The communists distributed the land to the peasants and built up a planned economy on the Soviet model. Mao's campaigns such as the Great Leap Forward and the Cultural Revolution later cost millions of people their lives.
koreakrieg#summary: North Korea's attack on the South leads to the first hot war of the Cold War, with millions of dead.
koreakrieg#text: In 1945 Korea had been divided along the 38th parallel into a Soviet and an American zone, out of which two hostile states emerged. On 25 June 1950 communist North Korea attacked the South with Stalin's approval; the United Nations, from whose Security Council the Soviet Union was absent at the time, sent troops under American command. After the landing at Incheon the UN forces advanced as far as the Chinese border, whereupon China intervened with hundreds of thousands of soldiers. The armistice of 1953 restored the old border; a peace treaty was never concluded. Around three million people died, and Korea remains divided to this day.
bandung-konferenz#summary: 29 Asian and African states meet in Indonesia and call for a path of their own between the blocs.
bandung-konferenz#text: At the invitation of Indonesia, India, Pakistan, Burma and Ceylon, representatives of 29 states, together representing more than half of the world's population, came together in Bandung in April 1955. Jawaharlal Nehru, Sukarno, Gamal Abdel Nasser and China's prime minister Zhou Enlai condemned colonialism and racism, called for respect for sovereignty and rejected alignment with the military blocs. For the first time the conference gave the decolonized countries a common voice in world politics. Out of it grew the Non-Aligned Movement in Belgrade in 1961, which still exists today.
montgomery-busboykott#summary: The arrest of Rosa Parks sets off a boycott lasting 381 days and makes Martin Luther King the leader of the civil rights movement.
montgomery-busboykott#text: On 1 December 1955 the seamstress Rosa Parks refused to give up her seat on a bus to a white passenger in Montgomery, Alabama, and was arrested. The city's black community thereupon decided to stop using the buses; for more than a year tens of thousands walked or organized car pools. The 26-year-old pastor Martin Luther King led the boycott and became the spokesman of nonviolent resistance to racial segregation. In November 1956 the Supreme Court declared segregation on buses unconstitutional. The success encouraged sit-ins, freedom rides and the March on Washington in 1963, which led to the civil rights and voting rights acts of 1964 and 1965.
sputnik-1957#summary: The Soviet Union sends the first artificial satellite into space and triggers the Sputnik shock in the West.
sputnik-1957#text: On 4 October 1957 a Soviet rocket carried the 84-kilogram metal sphere Sputnik into orbit around the earth; radio amateurs all over the world could pick up its beeping. For the United States this was a shock, because the same rocket could carry nuclear warheads across the ocean, and the Soviet Union appeared to be technically superior. In 1958 Washington founded the space agency NASA and invested massively in science and education. The race into space brought the first human being into space with Yuri Gagarin in 1961, the American Moon landing in 1969, and satellites for weather, television and navigation.
afrikanisches-jahr-1960#summary: In a single year 17 African colonies become independent states.
afrikanisches-jahr-1960#text: After Ghana under Kwame Nkrumah had gained independence in 1957 as the first colony south of the Sahara, France in 1960 released almost all of its African territories from Senegal to Madagascar into independence; Nigeria, Somalia and the Belgian Congo also became independent. The United Nations admitted 17 new members and adopted a declaration against colonialism. But the borders of the colonial era, weak institutions and the interference of the superpowers weighed on the young states: in the Congo a civil war broke out immediately, in the course of which the first prime minister Patrice Lumumba was murdered in 1961. The settler colonies in the south, such as Algeria, Angola and Rhodesia, still had to win their freedom in long wars.
bau-der-berliner-mauer#summary: On 13 August 1961 the GDR seals off West Berlin and puts an end to the flight of its citizens to the West.
bau-der-berliner-mauer#text: By 1961 almost three million people had left the GDR by way of open Berlin. With Moscow's consent, the SED leadership under Walter Ulbricht had streets torn up and barbed wire strung during the night of 13 August; a concrete wall with a death strip soon followed. Families were separated overnight, and at least 140 people died at the Berlin Wall. It became the symbol of the Cold War and of the division of Europe.
kubakrise#summary: Soviet missiles in Cuba bring the world to the brink of nuclear war for thirteen days.
kubakrise#text: In October 1962 American reconnaissance aircraft discovered launch pads for Soviet medium-range missiles in Cuba. President Kennedy imposed a naval blockade and demanded their withdrawal. After days of tension Khrushchev gave in; in return the United States pledged not to attack Cuba and secretly withdrew missiles from Turkey. The crisis led to the establishment of the hotline between Washington and Moscow and, in 1963, to the first agreement on nuclear testing.
vietnamkrieg#summary: The United States intervenes in Vietnam with hundreds of thousands of soldiers and suffers its first defeat in a war.
vietnamkrieg#text: After the victory of the Viet Minh over France in 1954, Vietnam was divided into a communist North under Ho Chi Minh and a South supported by the West. In order to halt the advance of communism in Southeast Asia, the United States sent ground troops from March 1965 onward and bombed the North; at the peak more than 500,000 American soldiers were in the country. Despite superior technology they were unable to defeat the Viet Cong guerrillas, and the television images of napalm and destroyed villages provoked protests worldwide. In 1973 the United States withdrew, and in 1975 the North took Saigon and united the country. Around 58,000 Americans and several million Vietnamese lost their lives.
kulturrevolution-china#summary: Mao Zedong mobilizes the young against the party, intellectuals and traditions; terror and chaos grip the country.
kulturrevolution-china#text: In order to regain the power he had lost after the failed Great Leap Forward, Mao called on young people in 1966 to fight against bourgeois ideas and alleged traitors within the party. Millions of Red Guards waved the Little Red Book, publicly humiliated teachers, officials and artists, destroyed temples and books and deported the educated to the countryside for re-education; Deng Xiaoping too was stripped of power, and head of state Liu Shaoqi died in custody. Schools and universities remained closed for years, and the economy collapsed. Only Mao's death and the arrest of the Gang of Four in 1976 brought an end to the decade, which by some estimates cost more than a million lives. In 1981 the party declared it a catastrophe, but forbade any open examination of it.
prager-fruehling-1968#title: Prague Spring and the Year of Protest 1968
prager-fruehling-1968#summary: Warsaw Pact troops stifle the attempt at reform in Czechoslovakia, while in the West students rebel.
prager-fruehling-1968#text: Under its new party leader Alexander Dubček, Czechoslovakia attempted from January 1968 to create a socialism with a human face: censorship was lifted, travel permitted and economic reforms begun. During the night of 21 August around half a million soldiers of the Soviet Union and its allies marched in; the population offered nonviolent resistance, but the reforms were reversed, and the Brezhnev Doctrine declared such intervention to be the rule. In the same year students protested in Paris, Berlin, Berkeley and Mexico City against the Vietnam War, authoritarian structures and the silence of their parents' generation. 1968 became the symbol of a generation of new departures that changed society, universities and political culture.
mondlandung-1969#summary: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin become the first people to set foot on the Moon.
mondlandung-1969#text: After the Soviet Union had led the race into space with Sputnik in 1957 and Yuri Gagarin in 1961, Kennedy promised to put a human being on the Moon before the end of the decade. On 20 July 1969 the lunar module of Apollo 11 landed; around 600 million people watched live as Armstrong stepped onto the Moon. Five further landings followed up to 1972. The program brought advances in computer technology, materials and communications.
oelkrise-1973#summary: The Arab oil states cut production; prices quadruple, and the economic miracle comes to an end.
oelkrise-1973#text: During the Yom Kippur War in October 1973 the Arab OPEC states used oil as a political weapon against the supporters of Israel. In Western Europe and the United States there were fuel shortages, car-free Sundays and speed limits; inflation and unemployment rose. The crisis brought the postwar boom to an end and put energy saving, nuclear power and renewable energies on the political agenda.
iranische-revolution-1979#summary: The overthrow of the Shah turns Iran into an Islamic republic under Ayatollah Khomeini.
iranische-revolution-1979#text: In 1978 millions of Iranians took to the streets against the dictatorship, the westernization and the social inequality under Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi; clergy, students, merchants and the left united in protest. In January 1979 the Shah left the country, in February the cleric Ruhollah Khomeini returned from exile and had an Islamic republic proclaimed by referendum, in which the word of the supreme religious leader stands above all laws. The occupation of the American embassy in Tehran, with 444 days of hostage-taking, destroyed relations with the United States, and the Iraqi attack in 1980 led to an eight-year war. The revolution gave political Islam a boost worldwide and triggered the second oil crisis.
reaktorkatastrophe-tschernobyl#summary: The explosion of a Soviet nuclear reactor contaminates large parts of Europe with radiation and shakes confidence in nuclear power.
reaktorkatastrophe-tschernobyl#text: During a botched test on 26 April 1986, reactor block 4 of the Chernobyl nuclear power plant in Ukraine exploded; burning graphite hurled radioactive material kilometers into the air. The Soviet leadership kept silent for days, and only measurements in Sweden forced it to disclose what had happened; the town of Pripyat and a zone of 30 kilometers were evacuated, and hundreds of thousands of clean-up workers were exposed to high levels of radiation. The radioactive cloud came down over Belarus, Scandinavia and Central Europe, where playgrounds were closed off and vegetables destroyed. The disaster reinforced Gorbachev's policy of openness, strengthened the anti-nuclear movement and led several countries to phase out nuclear energy.
fall-der-berliner-mauer#summary: On 9 November 1989 the GDR opens the border; the peaceful revolution puts an end to the division of Germany.
fall-der-berliner-mauer#text: Mass flight by way of Hungary and the Monday demonstrations in Leipzig put the SED leadership under pressure in the autumn of 1989. When politburo member Günter Schabowski announced new travel regulations on the evening of 9 November, tens of thousands streamed to the border crossings, and the border guards raised the barriers. The communist regimes also fell in Poland, Hungary, Czechoslovakia and Romania. On 3 October 1990 the GDR acceded to the Federal Republic.
aufloesung-der-sowjetunion#summary: The Soviet Union breaks apart into fifteen independent states; the Cold War is over.
aufloesung-der-sowjetunion#text: Gorbachev's reforms had created freedoms but had not solved the economic crisis; the Baltic republics and others demanded independence. In August 1991 a coup by communist hardliners failed against the resistance gathered around Boris Yeltsin. On 8 December Russia, Ukraine and Belarus declared the union dissolved, and on 25 December Gorbachev resigned. Russia took over the legacy of the Soviet Union, including its nuclear weapons and its seat on the Security Council.
world-wide-web-1991#title: The World Wide Web Goes Public
world-wide-web-1991#summary: Tim Berners-Lee puts the first website online at CERN and makes the internet usable for everyone.
world-wide-web-1991#text: Since the 1970s the internet had connected computers at universities and in the military, but it could be operated only by specialists. From 1989 onward the British physicist Tim Berners-Lee developed at the CERN research center near Geneva a system consisting of web addresses, the transfer protocol HTTP and the page language HTML, with which documents could be linked worldwide. In August 1991 he made the first website public, in 1993 CERN released the technology free of charge, and with the Mosaic browser its triumphal progress began. Within a few years search engines, online commerce and social networks came into being; today more than five billion people use the network, which has fundamentally changed the economy, politics and everyday life.
jugoslawienkriege#summary: The break-up of Yugoslavia leads to the bloodiest wars in Europe since 1945, with expulsions and a genocide in Srebrenica.
jugoslawienkriege#text: After Tito's death and the end of communism, Slovenia and Croatia declared their independence in June 1991, and Bosnia and Herzegovina followed in 1992. Serbian nationalists under Slobodan Milošević sought to prevent this, and wars with mass expulsions, called ethnic cleansing, followed. Sarajevo was besieged for almost four years, and in July 1995 Bosnian Serb troops murdered around 8,000 Muslim men and boys in Srebrenica. The Dayton Agreement ended the Bosnian War at the end of 1995; in 1999 NATO intervened militarily in the Kosovo War without a UN mandate. A UN tribunal in The Hague later convicted many of those responsible.
wirtschaftsreformen-indien-1991#summary: In a severe balance-of-payments crisis, India opens its state-directed economy to the market and the world market.
wirtschaftsreformen-indien-1991#text: Since independence India had steered its economy with planning targets, high tariffs and a dense web of state licenses. In 1991 the country faced insolvency because its foreign exchange reserves covered only a few weeks of imports. The government of Prime Minister Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Manmohan Singh then lowered tariffs, abolished many licensing requirements and admitted foreign investment. In the following decades the Indian economy grew strongly, especially in software and services around cities such as Bangalore.
vertrag-von-maastricht#summary: Twelve European states found the European Union and decide on a common currency.
vertrag-von-maastricht#text: On 7 February 1992 the twelve members of the European Community signed a treaty in the Dutch town of Maastricht that raised their cooperation to a new level. When it came into force on 1 November 1993 the European Union was born, meant to cover not only the economy but also foreign, security, justice and home affairs. The treaty introduced citizenship of the Union and laid down the path to economic and monetary union, from which the euro emerged in 1999. In Denmark ratification at first failed in a referendum, and only after exemptions did the Danes approve it in 1993.
ende-der-apartheid#title: End of Apartheid and the Election of Mandela
ende-der-apartheid#summary: Nelson Mandela is elected president in South Africa's first free elections.
ende-der-apartheid#text: From 1948 onward South Africa's white minority had stripped the black majority of its rights and segregated it spatially through the system of apartheid. International sanctions, protests and the resistance of the ANC forced President de Klerk in 1990 to release Mandela and to repeal the racial laws. In April 1994 all South Africans were allowed to vote for the first time; the ANC won, and Mandela became president. A Truth and Reconciliation Commission examined the crimes of apartheid.
nafta-und-zapatisten#summary: Mexico, the United States and Canada form a free trade area, and on the same day Indigenous rebels rise up in Chiapas.
nafta-und-zapatisten#text: On 1 January 1994 the North American Free Trade Agreement, NAFTA, came into force, gradually removing tariffs between the United States, Canada and Mexico. On the same day the Zapatista Army of National Liberation occupied towns in the southern Mexican state of Chiapas. The predominantly Indigenous fighters protested against poverty, the loss of land and the consequences of free trade for small farmers. After brief fighting the conflict turned into negotiations, and the Zapatistas became a symbol of worldwide criticism of globalization. NAFTA greatly increased trade and was replaced by a new agreement in 2020.
voelkermord-ruanda#summary: Within about 100 days Hutu militias murder some 800,000 Tutsi and moderate Hutu while the world looks on.
voelkermord-ruanda#text: The Belgian colonial power had divided the population of Rwanda into Hutu and Tutsi and favored the Tutsi minority; after independence in 1962 discrimination and violence changed direction. When President Habyarimana's aircraft was shot down on 6 April 1994, the army, militias and incited neighbors began a planned campaign of murder, spurred on by radio stations that described the Tutsi as cockroaches. By July around 800,000 people had been killed with machetes and rifles, many of them in churches and schools to which they had fled. The United Nations even cut its peacekeeping force from about 2,500 to 270. Only the advance of the Tutsi rebels under Paul Kagame brought the killing to an end. An international tribunal later convicted those responsible, and the failure of the world community still shapes the debate about the responsibility to protect.
rueckgabe-hongkongs#title: Return of Hong Kong to China
rueckgabe-hongkongs#summary: Great Britain hands over its crown colony of Hong Kong to the People's Republic of China after more than 150 years.
rueckgabe-hongkongs#text: Hong Kong had been British since the First Opium War and had developed into one of the richest trading and financial cities in Asia. On 1 July 1997 Great Britain handed the colony over to China, which under the principle of one country, two systems guaranteed extensive self-government, a market economy and civil liberties for fifty years. At first Hong Kong remained an open economic center. After large pro-democracy protests in 2019, however, Beijing imposed a national security law in 2020 with which the opposition and the free press were largely suppressed.
putins-machtantritt#title: Vladimir Putin Becomes President of Russia
putins-machtantritt#summary: The former intelligence officer Putin takes power and gradually transforms Russia into an authoritarian state.
putins-machtantritt#text: After years of economic crisis, President Boris Yeltsin unexpectedly resigned on 31 December 1999 and made his prime minister Vladimir Putin acting head of state. Putin, who had made his name with a harsh approach in the Second Chechen War, won the presidential election in March 2000. Thanks to high oil and gas prices incomes rose, and many Russians valued the new stability. At the same time the Kremlin brought the major television channels under its control, persecuted opposition figures and weakened independent courts. A constitutional amendment of 2020 allows Putin to remain in office until 2036.
anschlaege-11-september#summary: Islamist terrorists fly hijacked aircraft into the World Trade Center and the Pentagon.
anschlaege-11-september#text: On 11 September 2001 nineteen attackers from the terrorist network al-Qaeda hijacked four passenger aircraft. Two brought down the Twin Towers in New York, one struck the Pentagon, and the fourth crashed in Pennsylvania after the passengers resisted. Almost 3,000 people died. The United States declared the war on terror, overthrew the Taliban regime in Afghanistan and invaded Iraq in 2003. Security checks and surveillance changed life all over the world.
china-tritt-der-wto-bei#title: China Joins the World Trade Organization
china-tritt-der-wto-bei#summary: By joining the WTO, China finally becomes part of world trade and rises to become the workshop of the world.
china-tritt-der-wto-bei#text: After fifteen years of negotiations the People's Republic of China became a member of the World Trade Organization on 11 December 2001. It undertook to lower tariffs and open its markets and in return gained access to the markets of the other members. Foreign companies relocated factories to China on a large scale, where millions of migrant workers from the villages produced clothing, electronics and toys for the world market. In 2010 China overtook Japan as the world's second-largest economy. In the United States and Europe, by contrast, many industrial jobs were lost, which later contributed to trade conflicts.
krieg-in-afghanistan#summary: After the attacks of 11 September a US-led coalition topples the Taliban, who return to power after twenty years.
krieg-in-afghanistan#text: Because the Taliban government gave shelter to Osama bin Laden and al-Qaeda, the United States and Great Britain began air strikes on Afghanistan in October 2001; by December the regime had fallen. An international security force, led by NATO from 2003 and including the German Bundeswehr, was meant to secure the building of a democratic state. But the Taliban regrouped and waged a long insurgency, while corruption weakened the government in Kabul. After an agreement between the United States and the Taliban, Western troops withdrew in 2021, and on 15 August 2021 the Taliban took Kabul.
einfuehrung-euro-bargeld#summary: In twelve EU states euro coins and notes replace the national currencies.
einfuehrung-euro-bargeld#text: The euro had been introduced as book money in 1999; on 1 January 2002 it came into circulation as cash and replaced the deutschmark, the franc, the lira and other currencies. Around 300 million people received a common currency that made trade and travel in Europe easier. The euro crisis from 2010 onward revealed the weaknesses of a currency without a common fiscal policy. Today more than 20 states use the euro.
gruendung-afrikanische-union#summary: The African states replace the Organization of African Unity with the African Union.
gruendung-afrikanische-union#text: The Organization of African Unity, founded in 1963, had supported decolonization but had hardly intervened in the internal affairs of its members, not even during the genocide in Rwanda. In July 2002 the African Union took its place in Durban, South Africa. It may intervene in member states in cases of genocide and serious war crimes and suspends members after military coups. The Union, headquartered in Addis Ababa, comprises 55 states, has sent peacekeeping troops to Somalia, for example, and in 2018 laid the foundation for an African free trade area.
unabhaengigkeit-osttimors#summary: After a long Indonesian occupation, East Timor becomes independent as the first new state of the 21st century.
unabhaengigkeit-osttimors#text: The former Portuguese colony of East Timor had been occupied by Indonesia in 1975; in the following decades more than 100,000 people died through violence, hunger and disease. In a vote organized by the United Nations in 1999, almost 80 percent of the population voted for independence. Pro-Indonesian militias then devastated large parts of the country until an international force led by Australia intervened. After a transitional United Nations administration, East Timor became independent on 20 May 2002, with the former resistance leader Xanana Gusmão as its first president.
entschluesselung-menschliches-genom#summ: The international Human Genome Project presents the sequence of the roughly three billion building blocks of human DNA.
entschluesselung-menschliches-genom#text: The Human Genome Project began in 1990 as a collaboration between research institutions in the United States, Great Britain, Japan, France, Germany and China. Its goal was to determine the sequence of the roughly three billion base pairs in the human genome. After a first draft in 2001, the project was completed in April 2003, faster and more cheaply than planned. Among other things it showed that humans have only about 20,000 genes, far fewer than expected. The results form a basis for research into hereditary diseases, for cancer medicine and for genetic testing, but they also raised questions about data protection.
irakkrieg#summary: A US-led coalition topples Saddam Hussein, but Iraq sinks into insurgency and civil war.
irakkrieg#text: The US government under George W. Bush justified the attack on Iraq above all with alleged weapons of mass destruction that were never found. Without a mandate from the UN Security Council and against the opposition of states such as Germany and France, American and British troops invaded in March 2003 and toppled Saddam Hussein within a few weeks. A bloody insurgency and fighting between Shiites and Sunnis followed, in which tens of thousands of civilians died. The United States withdrew its troops in 2011. The so-called Islamic State later emerged from underground groups in Iraq.
eu-osterweiterung-2004#title: Eastward Enlargement of the European Union
eu-osterweiterung-2004#summary: Ten states, including eight formerly communist countries of Central and Eastern Europe, join the EU.
eu-osterweiterung-2004#text: On 1 May 2004 Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia, Malta and Cyprus joined the European Union. It was the largest enlargement in its history and politically overcame the division of Europe by the Cold War as well. The accession countries had first had to establish democracy, the rule of law and a market economy according to the so-called Copenhagen criteria. Romania and Bulgaria followed in 2007, and Croatia in 2013. The enlargement brought growth and new freedoms, but also disputes over labor migration and the rule of law.
tsunami-im-indischen-ozean#summary: An undersea earthquake off Sumatra triggers a tsunami that kills around 230,000 people in fourteen countries.
